en: The *Buddha-spoken Sūtra on the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper for Prolonging Life*,
brought to this land by a Brahmin monk and received during the Tang Dynasty.
If a person is born under this star, they will be born among those who eat millet for their livelihood.
If one encounters misfortune, it is appropriate to make offerings to this sutra and carry the talisman of one's natal star;
this will bring great auspiciousness. [This applies to those] born in the mouth (mouth) and those born in the hour of the pig (hai).
They will descend to be born under this same star.
For those who subsist on millet and encounter misfortune, it is appropriate to make offerings to this sutra and to wear the talisman of the presiding star.
Greatly auspicious.
Those born in the Tiger (Yin) or Dog (Shu) positions are likewise born under this star.
For those whose livelihood depends on eating non-glutinous rice,
it is auspicious to make offerings to this sutra and carry the talisman of their natal star during times of misfortune;
this will bring great good fortune.
Those born in the second or seventh lunar month are both born under this star;
their sustenance consists of small beans.
If one encounters misfortune, it is appropriate to make offerings to this sutra and carry the talisman of one's natal star;
this will bring great good fortune.
This applies to those born under the *ho* (甲) and *shin* (申) stems.
They will descend to be born together under this star.
Their sustenance shall be hemp seeds.
If there is misfortune, one should make offerings to this sutra and carry the talisman of the presiding star.
Greatly auspicious.
For those born under the *hetu* mansion, whether already born or yet to be born,
they are all reborn under this same star.
For those whose lot is to consume large beans,
should they encounter misfortune, it is auspicious to make offerings to this sutra and carry the talisman of their natal star;
this will bring great good fortune.
Those born in the hour of the Horse are born under this star;
their sustenance is small beans.
If one encounters misfortune, it is appropriate to make offerings to this sutra and carry the talisman of one's birth star;
there will be great good fortune. Namo to the Star Tanlang.
This is the Tathāgata Buddha Yuni Tongzheng (Yunyi Tongzheng) of the most excellent world in the east.
Homage to the Great Gate Star (Jumenxing).
This is the Tathāgata Buddha Guanzizai (Guangyin Zizai) of the world of Wondrous Jewels (Miaobao) in the east.
Homage to the Star Luk-ts'un.
This is the Buddha, the Tathāgata Suvarṇasiddhi, of the Perfect World in the East.
Homage to the Star Wen-k'u.
This is the Buddha, the Tathāgata Most Victorious Auspiciousness, of the world Anāthā in the east.
Homage to the Constellation of Integrity.
This is the Buddha, the Tathāgata Vast Wisdom and Eloquence, of the world Pure Abode in the east.
Homage to the Martial Curvature Star.
This is the Tathāgata Buddha, Dharma-Ocean Play, of the World of Dharma-Intention in the East.
Homage to the Army-Breaking Star.
This is the Buddha, the Tathāgata Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, of the Vaiḍūrya World in the eastern direction.
If one encounters calamities or misfortunes during the course of one's life, one should prostrate seven times before this sutra.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī:
This sutra that has been taught possesses great majesty and great power;
it can rescue all sentient beings from their grave offenses and extinguish all karmic obstructions.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, officials, laymen,
or laywomen— whether noble or humble, whether large or small living beings— [who...]
All are governed by the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper.
If one hears this sutra, receives and upholds it, makes offerings to it, and recites it,
and further encourages friends, relatives, and kinsmen to receive and uphold it, they shall obtain blessings in the present life and attain rebirth in the heavens in future lives.
If a son or daughter of good family,
or those who have previously passed away,
should fall into hell or undergo various forms of suffering;
If one hears this sutra and, with faith and reverence, makes offerings to it,
then deceased relatives will immediately leave the hells and be reborn in the World of Ultimate Bliss. If there are good men or good women who...
Or if they are invaded by ghosts and demons, harassed by malevolent spirits,
or experience nightmares, strange portents, and the terror of their souls,
if they hear this sutra, receive and uphold it, and make offerings to it—
Thereupon, the soul and spirit shall attain peace and tranquility,
and one shall forever be free from fear. If there are good men or good women who serve in office,
perform corvée labor, or set out on military expeditions;
If one encounters this sutra and offers it with faith and reverence,
one will immediately attain a high promotion in official service, which is most greatly auspicious.
If a good man or a good woman is afflicted by illness of the body...
If one desires to seek swift recovery from illness, one should burn incense and make offerings to this sutra in a clean room;
then the disease will be healed. If there are good men or good women...
If one wishes to achieve advancement and success in business affairs,
seeking wealth with full fulfillment through trade and commerce,
and should encounter this sutra, they should believe in, revere, and make offerings to it.
One will immediately obtain the wealth sought and have one’s endeavors fulfilled; there will be great good fortune in all comings and goings.
If there are good men or good women who raise silkworms and suffer losses, or whose six domestic animals are restless and uneasy, [they shall likewise find relief].

If one burns incense in a pure room to make offerings to this sutra, one will immediately find that one’s agriculture and sericulture fulfill their intentions, and domestic animals will multiply and flourish;
there shall be no loss whatsoever, nor any calamities or obstacles. If there is a woman whose pregnancy has reached the difficult month [of childbirth], [she shall likewise find relief].
If one encounters this sutra and offers it worship with faith and reverence,
immediately upon doing so, the mother and child will be separated from calamities and hardships,
and all children born shall likewise be spared.
All shall obtain the retribution of physical excellence and long life.
Good sons and good daughters should know that the seven stars of the Northern Dipper govern the lives of human beings and all calamities and misfortunes encountered throughout one's lifetime.

Regarding legal disputes, verbal strife, the clanging of cauldrons, and a hundred strange omens—if one encounters these and reverently believes in and makes offerings to this sutra, none of them shall cause any harm.
At that time, Mañjuśrī said: "If good men and good women respectfully believe in and accept it, prostrate themselves, and scatter [offerings], [they shall attain peace]."
The *Buddha-spoken Sūtra on the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper for Prolonging Life*, "The Seventeenth Determination of the Thin Grass," Part Two on the Annual Destiny.
I have fortunately obtained this scripture, a copy transmitted from the Hōkōdai at Tōnomine, at Fuku-shō-mitsu-ji Temple in the north of Kyoto.
The state was bestowed for the carving of printing blocks.

At that time, two years into the reign of Harmony (xianghe), in the second year of the Renxu cycle, during the month of midsummer, the śramaṇa Kuaidao recorded this at the Shōjiji Temple beneath the Rinsenbō Hall on Mount Hōzan. One proofreading and addition of notes completed by Jishun.
